newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - March 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - March 12.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

The Agriculture Minister Douglas Hogg has been called upon by Tony Blair to make a statement following claims that he was aware of investigations into the links between abattoirs and the E-coli virus, despite telling the Commons the opposite only days ago. Blair claims that letters from the independent Association of Meat Inspectors, which were leaked to Labour's agriculture spokesman, show that concerns about contamination were being made known to ministers over a period of nine months.
BANK CHIEF STIRS UP NEW EMU WORRIES

Howard Davies, the Deputy Governor of the Bank of England, made a speech to Tokyo bankers last night which expressed doubts about whether large European countries would be ready to join the single currency. He said the financial markets had already demonstrated doubts about the ability of Italy and Spain to join, and some of Davies' other comments could be interpreted as criticism of the French government's drive to qualify. --

The Securities and Futures Authority is investigating the apparent mishandling by SBC Warburg of the sale of 300 million stg of shares on behalf of Kepit, the liquidated investment trust. The investigation will focus on how the price of several of the stocks collapsed last October.
DEUTSCHE ACTS TO COOL RUSSIAN EUROBOND ROW

Deutsche Bank has attempted to calm down a row which broke out with the Russian government, following comments by a Deutsche Morgan Grenfell syndicate official that Russia's debut two billion mark (725 million stg) eurobond issue might have to be postponed because of poor market conditions. Deutsche stated that the bond will be issued on the German market as planned, but no final decision on timing had yet been reached, correcting the impression that the bank had made a unilateral decision not to launch the bond tommorrow.
